domain-willeke.name: willeke.com
domain-willeke.description: allowRelaying=true is safe only because of the relay-guard SieveSystemScript wired to MtaStageRcpt.script -- see stalwart-config/README.md "Split-delivery relay" section before touching either.

route-google-relay.name: google-willeke-com-relay
route-google-relay.description: Relay for @willeke.com mail via Google's SMTP relay, so Google's SPF/DKIM/DMARC for willeke.com apply.

sieve-relay-guard.name: relay-guard
sieve-relay-guard.description: Closes the relay-abuse gap that domain-willeke's allowRelaying=true opens: without this, any unauthenticated sender on :25 could RCPT to a made-up @willeke.com address and have Stalwart forward it out through google-willeke-com-relay using Scott's own smart-host credentials. Rejects RCPT for willeke.com when the address is not a member of the willeke-local-mailboxes MemoryLookupKey list AND the session is unauthenticated. Queries that list rather than hardcoding an address inline, or calling is_local_address(), because Sieve's function set (see stalw.art/docs/sieve/reference) exposes is_local_domain but no address-level directory lookup -- is_local_address only exists in the separate, non-Sieve config-expression engine used by fields like Domain.rewrite, and using it here fails to compile with 'Invalid variable or function name'. Provisioning a new real mailbox on this domain means adding a matching MemoryLookupKey record in the same namespace; this script never needs to change. Google's dual-delivery copy always arrives unauthenticated on :25 addressed to scott@willeke.com, already in the list, so it is unaffected; Scott's own submission traffic on :465 always carries authenticated_as (Stalwart disables SASL on :25 by default, see MtaStageAuth), so it always skips this rule and reaches the relay for any other willeke.com address. Wired via MtaStageRcpt.script. See stalwart-config/README.md "Split-delivery relay" for the full incident and design rationale.

sieve-forward-envelope-sender.name: forward-envelope-sender
sieve-forward-envelope-sender.description: Guards and rewrites an SMTP transaction addressed to micah@willeke.com. An unauthenticated session must come from Google's sending ranges (_spf.google.com), because that address is reached only through the Workspace routing rule, and port 25 is public: without the check anyone could send a forged From: that leaves through google-willeke-com-relay as willeke.com mail. Anyone else gets the same 550 relay-guard gives. It then rewrites the envelope sender to scott@willeke.com, the way a Google group rewrites it to its own bounce address. Neither recipient of the micah MailingList (an iCloud address and the oksanascott@willeke.com Google group) is a local mailbox, so both copies go out through google-willeke-com-relay, and smtp-relay.gmail.com accepts only envelope senders in our own domains, so an outside sender's address would be refused. Rewrites the whole transaction, so another local recipient in the same transaction gets a Return-Path of scott@willeke.com; nothing else changes. Selected by MtaStageRcpt.script in place of relay-guard. See stalwart-config/README.md "micah@willeke.com".
sieve-forward-envelope-sender.contents:
require ["variables", "reject", "vnd.stalwart.expressions"];

# Runs at RCPT for micah@willeke.com only (MtaStageRcpt.script).
#
# Port 25 is open to the internet, and the rewrite below makes whatever arrives here leave
# through smtp-relay.gmail.com as scott@willeke.com, DKIM-signed for willeke.com. So an
# unauthenticated sender must be Google, the MX, delivering through the Workspace routing
# rule; anyone else could write a forged From: and have it pass DMARC downstream. The
# ranges are _spf.google.com as of 2026-11-27. When Google changes them, update this list,
# or mail to micah@ from the new ranges is refused and Google bounces it to the sender.
if eval "is_empty(env.authenticated_as) && !(is_ip_in_cidr(env.remote_ip, '74.125.0.0/16') || is_ip_in_cidr(env.remote_ip, '192.178.47.0/24') || is_ip_in_cidr(env.remote_ip, '192.179.92.0/22') || is_ip_in_cidr(env.remote_ip, '209.85.128.0/17') || is_ip_in_cidr(env.remote_ip, '2001:4860:4864::/56') || is_ip_in_cidr(env.remote_ip, '2404:6800:4864::/56') || is_ip_in_cidr(env.remote_ip, '2607:f8b0:4864::/56') || is_ip_in_cidr(env.remote_ip, '2800:3f0:4864::/56') || is_ip_in_cidr(env.remote_ip, '2a00:1450:4864::/56') || is_ip_in_cidr(env.remote_ip, '2c0f:fb50:4864::/56'))" {
    reject "550 5.7.1 Relaying denied";
}

# The address is a MailingList, and none of its recipients is a local mailbox, so every
# copy leaves through smtp-relay.gmail.com, whose Allowed senders setting accepts only
# envelope senders in our own domains. Without this the envelope sender is whoever wrote
# to micah@ and the relay refuses it. scott@ owns the list, so bounces go to him.
set "envelope.from" "scott@willeke.com";

sieve-archive-all.name: archive-all
sieve-archive-all.description: Keep a copy of every delivered message in the account's \Archive mailbox, so deleting from the Inbox -- or iOS purging Trash after seven days -- does not destroy it. Import per account with: require ["include"]; include :global "archive-all";
sieve-archive-all.contents:
require ["fileinto", "copy", "mailbox", "special-use", "imap4flags", "spamtest", "relational", "comparator-i;ascii-numeric"];

# Spam goes to Junk and is deliberately NOT copied to the archive, so emptying Junk
# actually frees it. This branch is also load-bearing: Stalwart's own spam filing at
# ingest.rs:357 is guarded by `mailbox_ids == [INBOX_ID]`, an exact vector equality, and
# any fileinto below would break that equality and silently deliver spam to the Inbox.
# The threshold reproduces Stalwart's decision exactly -- is_spam() is
# `spam_percentage >= 50`, and spam_status() maps Ham to 1, MaybeSpam(pct) to
# ((pct*10) as i64).clamp(2,9), Spam to 10, Unknown to 0. So 49 -> 4 and 50 -> 5.
if spamtest :value "ge" :comparator "i;ascii-numeric" "5" {
    addflag "$Junk";
    fileinto "Junk";
} else {
    # Targeted by SPECIAL-USE rather than by name: whatever mailbox carries \\Archive
    # receives the copy, so renaming the folder -- or a user who named theirs something
    # else -- cannot silently break this. "Archive" is only the fallback name used when
    # :create has to make it.
    #
    # :copy leaves the implicit keep intact, so the message lands in BOTH Inbox and the
    # archive. That is one message in two mailboxes, not two copies: ingest takes a Vec of
    # mailbox ids on a single document, verified live twice -- once before the Phase 9
    # backfill and again on 2026-09-01 after it, as a JMAP Email/get returning mailboxIds
    # with both the inbox-role and archive-role mailbox set on one document. Resolve those
    # ids via Mailbox/get role, not by the numbers in an ingest log line: deleting the 14
    # Gmail artifact mailboxes during the backfill renumbered them. Deleting from
    # the Inbox, or iOS purging Trash after its default seven days, only untags one mailbox
    # -- expunge.rs destroys a message solely when mailboxes.len() == 1.
    fileinto :copy :specialuse "\\Archive" :create "Archive";
}
